clue.text: Wait on guests eating meat

indicators.note: the run of words 'Wait on guests' is eating, or holding inside it, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A waiter serves diners who are tucking into their meat course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' signals the answer is held inside 'waiT ON GUEsts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox or lamb's tongue is cooked and sold as a cut of meat, so it is an example of meat.

clue.text: Funny sort of female leaving trunk

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters that remain are put into an odd order
the letter for female is leaving the words, so it is taken out of them

explanation.surface: An odd kind of woman walks away from a large travelling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes F from SORTOF, giving SORTO; 'Funny' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of a body is the torso: the part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Services range between Norway and Middle East

indicators.note: the range sits between the two other pieces, Norway's letter and the East piece

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

indicators.note: Middle asks for the central letters of the word East

parts.note: a kitchen range is a cooking stove with an oven

explanation.surface: A geography lesson: some mountain range lying between Scandinavia and the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle East' looks like the region, but 'Middle' takes AS, the centre of EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Roman Catholic devotion of prayers over nine days, a kind of religious service.

clue.text: Complete a new church statement

parts.note: complete as in total or absolute, like utter nonsense
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off a fresh announcement on behalf of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything spoken aloud, such as a remark or declaration, counts as a statement in this sense.

clue.text: Island hard on footwear, so I hear

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: so I hear says the word for footwear is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear

explanation.surface: Someone has heard that an island is tough on shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of Japan's islands, home to Tokyo; so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: One managed to collect paper — a lot

indicators.note: the shuffled letters gather up the paper, taking it inside them
managed as in handled or manipulated, so the letters of One are reworked

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper

explanation.surface: A person succeeded in gathering a great deal of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' reads as succeeded, but it is the signal to rearrange; 'paper' is the Financial Times, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something frequently is doing it a great deal, so the adverb phrase means frequently.

clue.text: McCartney, king of the stars

parts.note: Stella McCartney is the fashion designer, daughter of Paul McCartney
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Beatle is crowned monarch of the celebrity world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'McCartney' suggests Paul; it is his daughter Stella, the designer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to stars, from the Latin stella, star.

clue.text: Most uncharitable type occupies posh birthplace

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

indicators.note: the type word occupies, or fills, the birthplace word

parts.note: a nest is where birds are hatched
a kind is a type or sort

explanation.surface: A certain sort of person takes over an upmarket place of birth and proves mean.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes Shakespeare's 'the most unkindest cut of all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of unkind: the cruellest, least generous of all.

clue.text: Go on to enlist fourth ranker

indicators.note: to enlist is to take in as a recruit, so the fourth piece is drawn inside

parts.note: to go on is to talk at length, to prate
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: An instruction to sign up the fourth person in a queue of army recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is a soldier in the ranks rather than an officer; the lowest rank is the private.

clue.text: Beef about rare variable sort of bacon

indicators.note: the beef word goes about, or around, the letter for rare

parts.note: steak is a cut of beef
R can stand for rare
Y is an algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A cook frets over rare beef and an unpredictable kind of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon with alternating stripes of fat and lean is described with this word, a type of bacon.

clue.text: Seeking success, limits debts

parts.note: an ambit is a scope or bounds, its limits
IOUs are written promises to pay, acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A go-getter's financial chase is constrained by what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aspiring hard to achieve, keen to get on, is described this way.

clue.text: Show up north adopts a foreign test for rustics

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the outer pieces enclose the others

parts.note: to show up is to come or arrive
un is French for a
a try is a test or attempt

explanation.surface: A northern show adopts an exotic trial run for country folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show up' reads like reveal or reversal; it simply means arrive, COME.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustics are people from rural areas, the sense of country folk as opposed to townies.

clue.text: Advance large target

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an end is an aim or target

explanation.surface: An army moves forward towards a big objective.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to loan it, a synonym.

clue.text: Box office star who controls crew?

parts.note: the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: A film star with box-office pull directs the production crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' suggests film crew; it is a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain is the ship's officer in charge of the deck crew and equipment.

clue.text: Officer's new bride investing capital

indicators.note: investing as in clothing or enveloping, so the rearranged bride surrounds the capital
new signals a new form of the letters of bride

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: An officer's young wife puts money into the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' suggests finance; here it means clothing or wrapping around, and 'new' rearranges the bride's letters so they split around the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army officer commanding a brigade, ranked above colonel.

clue.text: Italian team, embarrassed, stuck in ground

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: An Italian football side, red-faced, gets bogged down on a muddy pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Burial puts a body into the earth, so the dead are placed in the ground.

clue.text: Book-keeper bound to bring up reserves after a short time

indicators.note: after places the reserves construction behind the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: reserves means holds or keeps, so the bring-up word keeps the bound word inside

parts.note: to rear is to bring up a child
bound as in certain, sure to happen

explanation.surface: An accountant certain to reveal the reserve funds before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserves' looks like a noun (funds); it is the verb, REAR holding SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who keeps a club's or society's accounts is its money officer, a book-keeper.

clue.text: PM's detective touring state

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the detective goes around the state

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
Israel is a state in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A prime minister's police officer travels around a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Where to conduct or conversely play banjo?

indicators.note: conversely means the other way round, so the little word or is read backwards

parts.note: to strum is to play a banjo or guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: A musician wonders whether to conduct the orchestra or just pick up a banjo.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor stands on a raised platform, the podium, to direct the players.

clue.text: Cut back court demand

indicators.note: back means the cut word is read backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A legal claim is slashed in return for a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on and obtain payment is to demand it, as in exact a fee.

clue.text: Ace left crew to crack IT problem

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: to crack is to break open, so the left and crew pieces split the word IT

parts.note: men make up a crew

explanation.surface: A top expert quit the team brought in to fix a computer problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT problem' reads as a computing fault; IT is just letters for the crew to break into.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor illness, a health problem or complaint.

clue.text: Auditors get across all except odd features

indicators.note: taking all the letters except those in odd positions leaves the even ones of get across

explanation.surface: Accountants see past everything except the strange characteristics of a set of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' suggests accountants; here it means organs that listen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is literally a hearer, and the organs of hearing do the listening.

clue.text: Puzzle fans and chop suey lovers

indicators.note: chop means cut up, so the letters of suey lovers are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A list of the solvers and people fond of a Chinese takeaway dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chop suey' reads as the dish, but 'chop' is the anagram signal on SUEY LOVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter addresses the solvers directly: the puzzle fans are you, the readers.

clue.text: Long story involving European

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the story word wraps around the European letter

parts.note: a yarn is a story or tale

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale with a European in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to pine.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it.

clue.text: Bush's foreign articles

parts.note: foreign colours both articles: el is a Spanish word for the
der is a German word for the, so both pieces are foreign definite articles

explanation.surface: A US president's writings published abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the president; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or small tree with white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Ring about vessel moving about in daylight

indicators.note: about means around, so the ring word goes around the vessel

parts.note: to dial is to ring on the telephone
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A circle around a ship that is sailing in daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals active by day rather than at night are called this, the opposite of nocturnal.

clue.text: Intimates following one in tears

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the one letter is put in the tears word

parts.note: rends means tears or rips
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Close friends trailing after someone who is crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping; it is rips, RENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimates are close companions, those one is close to.

clue.text: Book gypsy with Poles

parts.note: Roma is the name for the Romani people, the gypsies
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Reserve a traveller's place alongside some Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; it is the magnetic poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Romans is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: He addresses men twice at breaks

indicators.note: breaks means comes between, splitting the doubled men pair
twice means the men abbreviation is written two times

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A man gives speeches to soldiers during their twice-daily rest periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addresses' suggests postal addresses; it means gives speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker who delivers addresses or formal speeches.
